verdict.rationale: Gumroad publishes the full source of its web application on GitHub, invites forking, and documents a local setup that runs the Rails server, JS build, and Sidekiq worker, so self-hosting the core product is possible. Community reports show real limits: the license is source-available rather than open source and caps use at $1M in revenue, and running the app requires relationships with many third-party vendors (Stripe/PayPal, TaxJar, SendGrid, etc.). Missing for 10: a documented production self-hosting/deployment guide (the setup shown is development-oriented), a permissive license without the revenue cap, independent hands-on reports of a successful self-hosted deployment, and a self-host path that does not depend on numerous third-party vendors.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: This repository contains the source code for the Gumroad web application.
This starts the Rails server, the JavaScript build system, and a Sidekiq worker.
One user liked that Gumroad's code license allows use up to $1M in revenue before you must rebuild.
